title: TSB contract graded_by side index
description: What each reference fixture is graded by, checked. A fixture's own `graded_by` says, in prose, which unit's test grades it; this file names that test, so a run can check it rather than take it on trust: an entry {unit, file, test_id} must appear with outcome pass in the results the run is given (`tsbc verify --provider-results`), and an entry {unit, owed} says no such test exists yet, which is never graded. A fixture's prose and its index may name the same test and disagree in detail — the prose is description, the index is what is checked — but an entry whose `unit` is not among the fixture's own `graded_by` units, an entry naming no fixture, or an entry for a fixture that is not graded `reference` is refused by self-check.
x-fixture-key: Fixtures are named `<seam>/<name>`, as in the README and in every fixture's path.

file.description: The test's file, repo-relative in the provider's repo. It is read as a path, never opened: it may not begin with `/` and may hold no `..` segment, which `tsbc`'s own path rules refuse in every input it takes. The unit-to-directory check is the provider's.

test_id.description: The test's id within its file: a Go `TestName` or `TestName/sub`, the pytest node id after the file (`Class::test` or `test`), or a harness rig `rig-<name>`. A pytest test that is parametrized is cited without its `[param]` suffix; every parametrized case that ran must have passed.

owed.description: The plan that owes the test. An owed entry is never graded: an owed entry alone makes the fixture it sits on UNGRADED, never green; a named test on the same fixture that ran and failed still fails it.
